rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: material is equal, but your a4 pawn is passed and far from the other pawns. It is an outside passed pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.e2: Black's king must stop that pawn and goes far from the other side. Meanwhile, your king goes to capture the black pawns left undefended.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.l0: The pawn advances to a5 and calls the black king to the queenside.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.l1: Defence: the black king goes to c5, towards the pawn. If it lets the pawn run, it promotes.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.l2: Attack: the pawn advances to a6 and drags the black king even closer to the edge.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.l3: The black king goes to b6, next to the pawn, to capture it.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.l4: Your king goes to e4 and attacks the e5 pawn, which has lost the black king's protection.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.l5: Black captures the a6 pawn, but the black king is left on the edge, far from the pawns on the other side.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex1.l6: The white king captures on e5 and then captures the g4 pawn. The outside pawn was a decoy: it cost one pawn and won two.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: the black king threatens to capture the f3 pawn. You have the outside passed pawn on a3, and the d4 pawn is within reach of your king.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.e2: Think before moving: capture on d4 or advance the a3 pawn? Count the square of the pawn after the advance.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.p: Play as White: the king or the pawn?
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes. With the pawn on a4, the black king on f4 is outside the square: it must chase the pawn and give up the f3 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the pawn advance to a4: the black king on f4 is outside the square and must chase it.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3d4.1: The king captures on d4, but the a3 pawn stays put, and the black king is still close to f3.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3d4.2: Black's attack: the king captures on f3, and the g5 pawn is free to run. Now it is Black who wins.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3d4.3: Back to the position: use the outside pawn to pull the black king away from f3.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3d2.1: The king goes to d2, but the a3 pawn stays put, and the black king is still free to capture the f3 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3d2.2: After this move, Black has a resource: the king captures on f3, and the g5 pawn is free to run. The win slips away.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3d2.3: Back to the position: use the outside pawn to pull the black king away from f3.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3e2.1: The king goes to e2, near the f3 pawn, but the a3 pawn stays put.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3e2.2: Defence: the d4 pawn advances with check. Black gives up that pawn to gain a tempo.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3e2.3: Your king captures on d3 and moves away from the f3 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3e2.4: The black king captures on f3, and the g5 pawn is free to run. The win slips away: the position is a draw.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.err.d3e2.5: Back to the position: use the outside pawn to pull the black king away from f3.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.fora: With that move, the black king is free to attack the f3 pawn. Look for the move that forces it to chase the a3 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: the king or the pawn?
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l1: Defence: the black king gives up the f3 pawn and enters the square on e5. Had it captured on f3, the a4 pawn would promote.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l2: Attack: the pawn advances to a5 and pulls the black king further aside.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l3: The black king goes to d5, still protecting the d4 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l5: The black king goes to c6 to stop the pawn, but gives up the d4 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l6: Your king captures the d4 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l7: Defence: the black king goes to b6 to capture the a6 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l8: Attack: meanwhile, your king goes to e5, heading for the g5 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l9: Black captures the a6 pawn, but the black king is stuck on the edge.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l10: The white king attacks the g5 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l11: The black king heads back to the centre, but it is too far away to defend the pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.ideia.ex2.l12: The king captures on g5, and the f3 pawn will run to promotion. The outside pawn moved first and pulled the black king away from f3.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.1: Defence: now the outside passed pawn belongs to Black, the h4 pawn. Your king is close to the c4 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.2: Think before moving: does the king capture on c4 or go to the square of the h4 pawn?
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.3: The king enters the square on e4. Capturing on c4 would let the h4 pawn run: the c4 pawn can wait.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.4: Black's attack: the pawn advances to h3, and the square shrinks: now it goes from h3 to f1.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.5: Your king follows the pawn and enters the square again, on f3.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.6: The pawn reaches h2, one square from promotion.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.7: The king goes to g2, controls h1 and will capture the pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.8: The black king goes to f5, heading for the d4 pawn, because the h2 pawn is already lost.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.defesa.9: The king captures on h2, and the position is a draw. Against the opponent's outside pawn, defence starts by stopping the pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.1: Attack: Fischer against Larsen, Candidates Match, Denver, 1971. Material is equal, and White has the outside passed pawn on a4.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.2: See how the a4 pawn beats the opposition: even if the black king takes the opposition, it will have to leave to watch the pawn, and the white king gets in through the centre.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.3: The white king goes to d4, in the centre, close to both sides.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.4: Defence: the black king takes the opposition on d6, in front of the white king, to keep it out.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.5: Attack: the white king cannot get through the centre, so the pawn advances to a5. The black king must watch it and, sooner or later, step out of the white king's way.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.6: Black pushes the f7 pawn one square to take the e5 square away from the white king.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.8: The black king goes to c6, towards the pawn, and gives up the opposition.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.9: The pawn reaches a7, and the black king has to go all the way to b7 to stop it.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.10: The black king goes to b7, next to the pawn, to capture it.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.11: Attack: without the black king's opposition, the white king walks in via d5, heading for the black pawns.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.12: Black advances the h5 pawn to trade pawns and leave fewer targets for the white king.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.fischer.13: The white king goes to e6 and will capture the pawns on the other side while the black king wastes time with the a7 pawn. Larsen resigned.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.1: Attack: Black has the outside passed pawn on h5. But your c5 pawn is also passed and is protected by the b4 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.2: The black king cannot capture the c5 pawn, and your king is free to go after the h5 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.3: Your king goes to f4, heading for the h5 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.4: Defence: the black king goes to d5, on the way to c4, where it attacks the b4 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.5: Attack: your king attacks the h5 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.6: The black king goes to c4 and attacks the b4 pawn, which protects the c5 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.7: Your king captures on h5: Black's outside pawn is gone.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.8: The black king captures on b4, and the c5 pawn loses its protection.
rot.outsidePasser.demos.excecao.9: The pawn advances to c6, and the black king on b4 is outside the square. Against a protected passed pawn, the outside pawn loses its power as a decoy.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.valeAqui.enunc: Now you play. Black has the outside passed pawn on a4, and your g5 pawn is passed and protected by the h4 pawn. The king or a pawn? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.valeAqui.fim: Your king entered the square of the a3 pawn and will capture it. The pawns stayed put: the black king cannot capture the g5 pawn, and if it goes to capture the h4 pawn, the g5 pawn is free to run.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.valeAqui.err.g: The pawn goes to g6 and leaves the protection of the h4 pawn: the black king captures it, and the win slips away.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.valeAqui.err.h: The pawn goes to h5 and wastes a tempo: the black pawn on the a-file advances at once, and your king can no longer catch it.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.valeAqui.err.r: The king stays outside the square of the a4 pawn: the pawn runs to promotion, and your king cannot catch it.
The king does not enter the square of the a3 pawn: the pawn runs to promotion, and your king cannot catch it.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.isca.enunciado: Your g5 pawn is passed, and the black king on e5 is close to it. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.isca.fim: The pawn went to g6 and drew the black king to f6 to stop it. With the black king away from f4, your king captured the f4 pawn and will then capture the b5 pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.isca.err.rei: The king moves, but the g5 pawn stays put, and the black king remains close to the f4 pawn to defend it.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.isca.err.rei2: The king moves, but does not capture the f4 pawn, and the black king gains time to come back.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.isca.err.g7: The pawn goes to g7, but the black king captures it at once, and the f4 pawn is still standing.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.pretas.enuncia: Now with Black. Your a5 pawn is an outside pawn and ties the white king to a3. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.pretas.fim: The white king was stuck watching the a5 pawn, and your king captured the c3 pawn. Next it will go for the g5 pawn on the other side.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.pretas.err.a4: The pawn goes to a4 and comes within reach of the white king. White advances the g4 pawn and, when your king goes after the c3 pawn, the white king captures the one on a4: the win slips away.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.pretas.err.f5: The pawn goes to f5, but the g4 pawn captures it, and the white pawn is free to run.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.pretas.err.pea: The pawn move does not attack the c3 pawn, and White gains a tempo: the white king comes to protect it, or the g4 pawn runs.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.pretas.err.rei: The king moves, but does not attack the c3 pawn: the white king gains time to protect it.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.pretas.err.pea: The pawn move does not capture on c3, and the white king comes to protect the pawn.
rot.outsidePasser.pratica.pretas.err.rei: The king moves, but does not capture the c3 pawn, and the white king comes to protect it.
